newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH JAN-SEPT RETAIL SALES UP 3.8 PCT YR/YR.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH JAN-SEPT RETAIL SALES UP 3.8 PCT YR/YR.

text.p: The value of retail sales rose 3.8 percent year-on-year in January-September while wholesales rose 5.0 percent, the Federation of Finnish Commerce and Trade (KKL) said in a statement on Tuesday.
It said its members forecast four percent growth in the value of retail sales and five percent growth in the value of wholesales in 1997.
The value of daily goods sales rose 3.0 percent year-on-year in the first nine-months.
The value of department store sales surged 6.4 percent in January-September and hardware sales rose 5.0 percent.
Pharmacy sales soared 10.1 percent while alcoholic beverage sales dropped 5.1 percent due to unofficial imports of alcohol.
In wholesales, consumer goods sales rose 5.0 percent.
Car wholesalers registered a 23.5 percent year-on-year rise in the value of their January-September sales and wholesales of electronic components rose 15.0 percent, KKL said.
Alcoholic beverage wholesales slumped 39.5 percent in January-September, still depressed by an increase in unoffical alchol trade such as private imports from Russia and Estonia.
KKL said it expected the value of retail sales to rise 4.5 percent in December compared to the year-ago period. Consumers spend approximately three billion markka on Christmas shopping, it said.
